related.prompt: Is Ubuntu an Arch Linux derivative?

chain: Ubuntu is based on Arch Linux. (edit)
based_on ⊑ derivative_of: a distribution based on another is a derivative of it.
So Ubuntu is an Arch Linux derivative: yes.
Ubuntu is based on Arch Linux. (edit)
The edit replaces Ubuntu's base, so based_on Debian (which made Ubuntu derivative_of Debian) is gone; no distribution is derived from both Arch Linux and Debian.
So Ubuntu is not a Debian derivative: no.

notes: Dev-split ABox revision that carries subproperty (based_on ⊑ derivative_of in RELATIONS.md) and, through it, transitivity of derivative_of. Rewritten after review: the earlier edit (the Wii succeeds the Nintendo Switch) asked successor_of ⊑ released_after, but the model stores both release years, so 'was the Wii released after the Switch?' had a stored route back to 'no', and the transitivity question looped back to the stored 'the Wii U succeeded the Wii'. A reversal of release order always clashes with stored dates, so the record moved to Linux distribution lineage, where nothing dated or stored contradicts the edit: Arch Linux is an independent distribution, so making Ubuntu based on it closes no loop. Related near asks the subproperty (is Ubuntu an Arch Linux derivative? no, then yes); derivative_of is many-valued, so the question is yes/no rather than 'which distribution is Ubuntu derived from?', which would leave Debian as a fair answer for a model that stored that fact separately. Related far asks the same of Linux Mint, through the stored 'Linux Mint is based on Ubuntu' (transitivity of derivative_of; alt chain based_on ∘ derivative_of ⊑ derivative_of); its original is stored as 'based on Ubuntu, which is based on Debian'. Linux Mint Debian Edition is also derived from Debian, which leaves the answer yes (derivation is many-valued). The three derived queries follow the edit to the new base distribution and look up an unconnected fact about it: its package manager (APT to pacman), whether it has numbered stable releases (yes to no) and whether it was first released in the 1990s (yes to no; Debian 1993, Arch 2002); with the two related questions (no to yes) the yes/no items flip both ways. No binding: Ubuntu has no common second name, and 'Canonical's Ubuntu' is written so often (2,360 hits) that a Canonical description would be stored. Near unrelated: the base of Kali Linux (Debian), another Debian derivative; an edit that spreads 'based on Arch Linux' to Debian-based distributions would change it. Main-split records use Manjaro, elementary OS and Rocky Linux as subjects; Ubuntu is not a main-split subject. Related (2026-11-14, two per record): based_on has one axiom to a stored fact here (subproperty), used twice: near is the edit's (Ubuntu an Arch derivative, no to yes); far is the replaced fact's (Ubuntu a Debian derivative, yes to no, by the Arch/Debian exclusivity the encoding already holds). The Linux Mint question was a 2-hop transitivity chain and is dropped.
